title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_1**
Supreme, abiding beyond [all], beginningless, deeper than the deepest, the One who has entered manifoldly into the 'caves' [of beings] — the abode of all, present in all that moves and does not move: in You alone, Śambhu / Śiva / Paramaśiva (the absolute non-dual consciousness-Lord), do I take refuge.
**PS_2**
Bewildered and tossed about by the wheel of suffering that runs from dwelling in the womb to the agony of death, the disciple asked the Blessed One, Ādhāra, about the paramārtha (the supreme/highest reality or goal).
**PS_3**
The teacher answered him [in the manner of] the ādhārakārikā (Ādiśeṣa's base-verses Abhinavagupta recast); [now] Abhinavagupta sets forth that essence, through the vision of the Śaiva scripture [Śiva's teaching].
**PS_4**
By the abundant majesty of His own śakti (the Lord's dynamic power/energy), this fourfold aṇḍa (cosmic 'egg'/sphere) — distinguished as Śakti, māyā (the Lord's self-veiling power of differentiation), Prakṛti, and Earth (pṛthivī) — is brought into being by the Lord, in their several divisions.
**PS_5**
Within them [is] this universe, an unbroken succession of variegated bodies, organs, and worlds; and the enjoyer there, the embodied one, is none other than Śiva, who has [voluntarily] assumed the paśu (the bound/fettered soul ('beast')) condition.
**PS_6**
Just as a flawless crystal takes on the appearance of manifold colours [set near it], so too the Lord [takes on] the forms of gods, men, beasts, and trees.
**PS_7**
As the disc of the moon [reflected] in water moves when the water moves and stays still when it is still, so does this Self, the Great Lord, [appear to move and rest] amid the host of bodies, organs, and worlds.
**PS_8**
Just as Rāhu, though invisible [in himself], becomes manifest when he rests upon the disc of the moon, so this Self, though all-pervading, [becomes manifest] in the mirror of the intellect by taking on objects.
**PS_9**
Just as a face shines forth in a stainless mirror, so this [Self], whose very nature is light, shines forth in the principle of intellect made pure by the descent of Śiva's power.
**PS_10**
[That reality is] of the form of light, wholly complete, [yielding] great bliss through repose in its own Self, filled to overflowing with [the powers of] will, knowledge, and action, perfectly replete with infinite powers (śakti).
**PS_11**
That supreme reality (paratattva) which is free of all thought-constructs, pure, tranquil, without dissolution or arising — within it shines the world whose nature is the thirty-six tattva (ontological reality-principle (here the 36)).
**PS_12**
Just as in the surface of a mirror the variegated [image] of city, village, and the rest, [though] undivided [from the mirror], appears with [internal] divisions — distinct from one another and from the mirror itself —
**PS_13**
so too, from the utterly stainless awareness of the supreme Bhairava, this world, though devoid of [real] division [from Him], shines forth as divided both from one another and from Him as well.
**PS_14**
[The Lord] makes manifest the [pure] state of the tattvas — consisting of Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Vidyā — through the differentiated mode of the five powers (śakti).
**PS_15**
That supreme autonomy of the Great Lord, which accomplishes what is [otherwise] impossible — this is the Goddess, the māyā (the Lord's self-veiling power of differentiation)-power (māyāśakti), Śiva's self-veiling of His own Self.
**PS_16**
Through taking on māyā, consciousness becomes sullied, and the [free] Person becomes a bound soul (paśu (the bound/fettered soul ('beast'))), fettered by the force of Time (kāla), [limited] agency (kalā), and Necessity (niyati), and through Attachment (rāga) and [limited] Knowledge (vidyā).

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_17**
'Only now,' 'only some little [I can do],' 'only this,' 'this alone I know completely' — this sixfold kañcuka (the limiting 'sheaths' (kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla, niyati)) together with māyā is declared to be the inner [constitution] of the atomic [bound] self (aṇu).
**PS_18**
Like the husk lodged upon the grain of rice — [seeming] separate, yet [united with it] without [real] separation — that [bondage], however, attains purification by turning eagerly toward the path of Śiva.
**PS_19**
Prakṛti is the mere [equilibrium of] pleasure, pain, and delusion; then comes the inner organ (antaḥkaraṇa) — in order: intellect (buddhi, the faculty of determination), mind (manas, of conceiving), and ego (ahaṃkāra, of self-appropriation).
**PS_20**
Ear, skin, eye, tongue, and nose are the organs of knowledge [operating] upon sound and the rest; and again, voice, hand, foot, anus, and genitals are the organs of action.
**PS_21**
The object grasped by these [organs of knowledge], which is subtle and devoid of [gross] differentiation, is the fivefold tanmātra (the five subtle elements (sound, touch, etc.)): sound, touch, form [sight], taste, and smell.
**PS_22**
Through the combination of these [subtle elements], the gross object comes to be the fivefold set of [gross] elements: ether, air, fire, water, and earth.
**PS_23**
As the husk envelops the kernel of rice, so this creation, beginning with Prakṛti and ending in Earth, envelops consciousness (caitanya) in the form of 'the body.'
**PS_24**
Here the highest [innermost] covering is the impurity (mala); the subtle [covering] is the sheath beginning with māyā (kañcuka (the limiting 'sheaths')); the gross, outer [covering] is the bodily form. Thus the Self is wrapped in a threefold husk (kośa).
**PS_25**
Through [contact with] the darkness of ājñāna / ajñāna-granthi (ignorance; the 'knot' of ignorance), one perceives the Self — though it is one's own single essential nature — as the manifold variety of the grasped and the grasper.
**PS_26**
Just as syrup, molasses, raw sugar, lump-sugar, and the rest are nothing but sugar-cane juice [in different states], so all the differentiated states are of the one supreme Self, Śambhu / Śiva / Paramaśiva (the absolute non-dual consciousness-Lord).
**PS_27**
[The whole hierarchy] ending in the [pure-knowledge soul] vijñānākala, the inner controller (antaryāmin), the vital breath (prāṇa), the Cosmic Person (virāṭ), the body, the [class-]birth, and the [bodily] lump — all this is mere [practical] convention; in the highest sense (paramārtha) they simply do not exist.
**PS_28**
In the rope there is no snake, yet [the imagined snake] causes terror, even to the point of death. Great indeed is the power of error — it cannot, truly, be [easily] discriminated away.
**PS_29**
In just this way merit and demerit, heaven and hell, birth and death, pleasure and pain, and [the distinctions of] caste and life-stage — though unreal in [respect of] the Self — come to be by the force of delusion.
**PS_30**
This is that [primal] darkness: that, although [all] entities are nothing other than the Self by virtue of being illumined [by It], there yet arises this conceit of [their being] the non-self.
**PS_31**
This is darkness upon darkness, a great blister upon the boil: that in what is non-self — in the body, the vital breath, and the rest — there is the conceit of [their being] the Self.
**PS_32**
By [identifying with] the body, the vital breath, [their] awareness, and the manifold display of intellect, cognition, and [the inner] space, [the Self] wondrously enmeshes its own Self — like a spider [enwrapping itself] with its web.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_33**
And by the shining-forth of the majesty of His own knowledge, He unwraps His own Self [again]. Thus does Śambhu / Śiva / Paramaśiva (the absolute non-dual consciousness-Lord), Paramaśiva, spread out the wondrous play of bondage and liberation.
**PS_34**
Emanation, maintenance, and dissolution; waking and dream and deep sleep — these shine forth in that abode, the turīya / turya (the 'Fourth', state beyond waking-dream-sleep); yet even so [the Fourth] shines unveiled by them.
**PS_35**
Waking is [governed by] Viśva [the all-pervading], because of differentiation; dream is Taijasa [the luminous], because of the predominance of inner light; the deep-sleep state is Prājña [the wise], because of being a dense mass of knowledge; and beyond that is the Fourth (turya).
**PS_36**
Just as the vault of the sky is not [really] sullied by cloud, smoke, and dust, so the supreme Person remains untouched by the modifications of māyā (the Lord's self-veiling power of differentiation).
**PS_37**
When the space within one pot is filled with dust, the [spaces in] other [pots] do not [thereby] become sullied; just so are these individual souls (jīva), each partaking of its own differentiation of pleasure and pain.
**PS_38**
When the assemblage of [psychic] principles is calm He [seems] calm, when it is elated [He seems] elated, when it is deluded [He seems] deluded; but the Blessed One is not, in the highest sense (paramārtha), [truly] so.
**PS_39**
Having first dispelled that appearance of [the Self's] form in the non-self, the supreme Self [then] shatters the [contrary] error which [imputes] the form of the non-self to the Self.
**PS_40**
For the supreme yogin, thus fulfilled by the uprooting of this twin-delusion at its very source, there never arises any thought of anything further to be done.
**PS_41**
Earth, Prakṛti, and Māyā — this triad, fallen [merely] into the condition of objects-to-be-known, becomes, by the force of non-dual contemplation (advaita-bhāvanā), reduced to pure Being (sanmātra) alone.
**PS_42**
Just as girdle, earring, and bracelet are seen [simply] as gold once their distinctions are dropped, so, when distinctions are dropped, everything shines forth as pure Being alone.
**PS_43**
That supreme Brahman — pure, tranquil, non-dual in essence, the same [everywhere], whole [and complete], deathless, true — reposes in the radiant śakti (the Lord's dynamic power/energy) whose nature is light.
**PS_44**
[Brahman] is 'willed,' is 'known,' is 'brought to be' [only] through [that] radiant nature; yet that which remains [in itself] untouched [by such activity] amounts to a flower-in-the-sky [an unreal abstraction, if conceived apart from Śakti].
**PS_45**
By the conjoining [withdrawal] along the trident of the [three] powers (śakti), the whole [universe] is offered up [resorbed] by the God of gods into the supreme Lord, into the highest reality named Śiva.
**PS_46**
And then again, by the process of the unfolding of the five powers, that variegated triple aṇḍa (cosmic 'egg'/sphere) is emitted outward as well, [the Self] attaining its outward [manifest] form.
**PS_47**
Thus the God, setting in motion the mechanism of the wheel of powers as [an act of] play — 'I alone, of pure form, stand in the station of the lord of the great wheel of powers (śakti).'
**PS_48**
'In Me alone the universe shines, as pots and the like [shine] in a spotless mirror; from Me all streams forth, as the wondrous variety of dream [streams forth] from one asleep.'

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_49**
'I alone am of the form of all, as the body has [its] nature as hands, feet, and the rest; in all entities it is I alone who scintillate, like the very nature of light [shining in them].'
**PS_50**
'[Though I am] seer, hearer, smeller, [yet] devoid of body and organs, and [though] a non-doer, it is I alone who compose the varied [systems of] doctrine, scripture, and reasoning.'
**PS_51**
Thus, when the thought-construct of duality has dissolved, having overleapt the deluding māyā (the Lord's self-veiling power of differentiation), one becomes dissolved into Brahman — as water into water, as milk into milk.
**PS_52**
Thus, when the whole assemblage of principles has, through contemplation, come to be of the nature of Śiva — for one who beholds all as Brahman, what grief, what delusion [can there be]?
**PS_53**
The fruit of action, good or ill, [accrues] only through contact [identification] with false knowledge; for grievous is the fault of [such] contact — like the [false] charge of thieving [falling] even upon one who is no thief [merely from his keeping company with thieves].
**PS_54**
Those deluded ones who here cultivate the ignorance (avidyā) fashioned by worldly convention — they go on to birth and death, bound fast by the bolt-bar of merit and demerit.
**PS_55**
But the karman too, consisting of merit and demerit, heaped up during the time of ājñāna / ajñāna-granthi (ignorance), perishes by the force of the blaze of [liberating] knowledge — like cotton long accumulated [consumed in an instant by fire].
**PS_56**
Once knowledge is attained, even what has been done [does] not [tend] toward fruit; how then [can there be any further] birth for such a one? With the bondage of birth gone, he shines as the Sun that is Śiva, with his own rays.
**PS_57**
Just as a seed freed from husk, hull, and beard does not [any longer] produce a sprout, so too the Self, freed from the [threefold impurity of] aṇava [atomizing], māyīya, and kārma [malas], surely produces no sprout of [further] existence.
**PS_58**
The knower of the Self fears nothing from any quarter, for everything is his own form; nor does he grieve, since in the highest reality (paramārtha) there is no [such thing as] destructibility.
**PS_59**
From the hoard of jewels of the highest reality (paramārtha), grown firm in the deeply hidden treasury of the heart — [arising as] 'I alone am' — in [such] the state of the Great Lord, what misfortune, [and] for whom?
**PS_60**
mokṣa / kaivalya (liberation; aloneness/isolation) has no [particular] abode whatsoever, nor [is it] any going elsewhere; liberation is the cutting of the knot of ignorance — the becoming-manifest of one's own power (śakti (the Lord's dynamic power/energy)).
**PS_61**
He whose knot of ignorance is cut, whose doubt is gone, whose error is dispelled, whose merit and demerit are worn away — such a one is liberated even while still joined to a body.
**PS_62**
Just as a seed scorched by fire becomes incapable of sprouting, so karman burnt by the fire of knowledge does not bestow [further] birth.
**PS_63**
Through being a limited intellect, by the [karman-bound] imagining of a future body appropriate to one's deeds, consciousness, [thus] contracted, shines forth in that very [contracted manner] upon the destruction of this [present] body.
**PS_64**
If, on the other hand, [one should realize] the stainless awareness — which transcends all, consisting of [pure] knower and doer, all-expansive, of the form of light that neither sets nor rises, whose every resolve is true —

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_65**
— [the awareness that is] free of the measuring-out of space and time, fixed, imperishable, the Lord, perfectly complete, the sole author of the dissolution, arising, and arrangement of the manifold host of powers (śakti) —
**PS_66**
— [if one] should awaken to the Self as of the nature of Śiva, the excellent Ordainer of emanation and the rest — how could such a one be a transmigrant? For one [thus] all-pervading, whence or whither [any] passage [to another body]?
**PS_67**
Thus by reasonings too it is established that whatever action the knower [does] bears no fruit. [And] from the firm conviction 'this is not mine, but His [the Lord's],' there is indeed, in the world, no fruit [that binds him].
**PS_68**
Thus awakened, [offering up] all thought-constructs through the wind of contemplation, [the liberated one], pouring them as oblation into the kindled fire of the light of the Self, becomes [himself] made of light.
**PS_69**
Eating this or that, clad in whatever [comes to hand], tranquil, dwelling wherever [he may be] — the one who is the Self of all beings is liberated.
**PS_70**
Though he should perform a hundred thousand horse-sacrifices or [commit] a hundred thousand slayings of brahmins, the knower of the highest reality (paramārtha), being stainless, is touched neither by merits nor by sins.
**PS_71**
Free of pride, exhilaration, anger, lust, dejection, fear, greed, and delusion, without [recourse to] hymns of praise or ritual exclamations (vaṣaṭ), let him wander like one inert [insentient], his mind beyond disputation.
**PS_72**
This class [of afflictions] beginning with pride and exhilaration arises from the delusion of differentiation; how then could the awakening to the non-dual Self ever be touched by it?
**PS_73**
There is for him nothing whatever, separate [from himself], to be praised or to be offered in sacrifice; [so] would he be pleased by praise and the like? The liberated one is therefore beyond [the rites of] salutation and ritual exclamation.
**PS_74**
Sustained by the thirty-six tattva (ontological reality-principle (here the 36)), full of the lattice-windows [the apertures] of the bodily structure — his own body, or another's, or a pot or the like — that is for him the temple of the deity.
**PS_75**
And there he abides, worshipping the deity — the supreme Self, the great Bhairava-Śiva, conjoined with His own power (śakti) — with the pure substances [of offering] that are [nothing but] the [reflexive] awareness of the Self.
**PS_76**
For him who offers up the whole store of the great seeds [of differentiation] — the conceptual division into outer and inner — the fire-oblation (homa) takes place without effort, in the intensely blazing flame of consciousness.
**PS_77**
His meditation (dhyāna) never sets [is unceasing]; for this Blessed One emits the variegated forms — and that very [emitting] is [his] meditation: [the world] having the reality of what is sketched out by [his] resolve.
**PS_78**
And [the act] by which he revolves within [his own] inner awareness the entire series of worlds, the ordered array of principles, and the host of sense-organs — that is declared to be his recitation (japa).
**PS_79**
[The liberated one,] who sees all with an equal eye and who [thus] reflects upon [his own] consciousness — [a consciousness] delighting in the cremation-ground that is the universe, equipped with the imagined skull-staff (khaṭvāṅga) that is the body —
**PS_80**
— and who savours [the contents of] the skull-bowl held in his own hand — the fragment of the knowable [object] — brimming with the wine that is the essence of the universe: this is his [great] vow (vrata), both most hard to attain and [yet for him] easy to attain.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_81**
Thus, having attained [that reality] free of birth and destruction, named the supreme-real Great Lord (paramārtha-maheśvara), through the manifest light of [pure] perceiver-hood, he abides — his task accomplished — as he pleases.
**PS_82**
Whoever thus knows [the Lord] — all-pervading, declared to be the Self of all, with [all] manifoldness shaken off, [whose] supreme bliss is beyond compare — he becomes [wholly] made of That.
**PS_83**
Whether at a holy ford (tīrtha) or in the house of an outcaste, even with memory lost, [when] casting off the body — [already] liberated from the very moment of knowing — he attains mokṣa / kaivalya (liberation; aloneness/isolation), his grief slain.
**PS_84**
Resort to a holy ford [is] for [the gaining of] merit, [and] death-passage in the dwelling of an outcaste [is] for [going to] hell; but when there is no touch of the stain of merit or demerit, of what use is [any of] that?
**PS_85**
[Even] casting back the kernel of rice — once well separated from husk and hull — into the midst of husk-fragments does not make it [re-]identify with that [husk-]form again.
**PS_86**
Just so, consciousness, [once] separated from the cluster of sheaths (kañcuka (the limiting 'sheaths')), [though] it remain here [in a body] on account of [residual] habit-traces (saṃskāra), is liberated in Self and becomes free of [any further] touch by them.
**PS_87**
A gem, [even though] made spotless by the most skilled lapidary, [seems] sullied [while shut up] within the limiting casket; but upon the severance of [that] limiting condition (upādhi), its true nature (paramārtha) is [seen to be] limpidly clear.
**PS_88**
So [too], the cognition [of the Self], abiding in the purity [established] by the true teacher's instruction, though [still] freed [from bondage even while bound] by the limiting condition of the body, shines as the very form of Śiva — as if void of any [further] limiting condition.
**PS_89**
[One who,] even [merely] through unwavering faith [grounded] in the authority of scripture and the rest, has attained [some] state of being made of That — that very one [may] first [pass through] heaven, hell, [or] human birth.
**PS_90**
But the last moment [of life], in his case nourishing a meritorious or a sinful state, [merely] serves as a cooperating cause for the deluded [in determining their next destiny]; it is not the [true] cause of [that] destiny [for the knower].
**PS_91**
Even beasts, birds, reptiles, and the like, who know [the Self] as their own self [and so know] their own [true] goal — they too, refined by an awakening [acquired] in former [births], attain that goal.
**PS_92**
This Person, abiding in the interior of a body, [becomes] of the nature of heaven or of the nature of hell; and when that [body] breaks up, he passes, in accordance with his own fitness, to union with another body.
**PS_93**
Thus, in whatever manner his own Self once shone forth to him at the moment of knowing, in just that manner [he then is]; and at the falling away of the body he does not become otherwise.
**PS_94**
The failing of the host of organs, the loss of memory, the choking thickness of breath [and its] cutting-off, the special pangs in the vital points — [all this] is [merely] an experience [bhoga] arising from the conditioning of the body.
**PS_95**
How should that [experience] not occur for one [still] joined to a body? Yet, even with [such] an accompaniment of bewilderment, the knower, at the hour of death, does not fall away from the highest reality (paramārtha) of his own Self.

title: Paramārthasāra
text:
**PS_96**
When one approaches this path of the highest reality (paramārtha) swiftly, from the mouth of the teacher, through an exceedingly intense śaktipāta (the 'descent of power' / divine grace), then at that very moment, without any obstacle, he [becomes] Śiva.
**PS_97**
For one who resorts, by the gradual ascent of the steps of a stair, to the form that transcends all — upon attaining firm establishment in the supreme reality (paratattva), there is at the end the becoming made of Śiva.
**PS_98**
But for one who has not [yet] reached the stream that is made of the highest reality (paramārtha) — that is, the repose in the centre — even though his mind be eager for the attainment of that station, death may [nonetheless] come at some time [before completion].
**PS_99**
He is called in the scripture the yogabhraṣṭa (the yogin 'fallen' from practice before completion), [and becomes] a lord of wondrous worlds of enjoyment; and [then], by the power of [his attained] place of repose, he becomes Śiva in a later birth.
**PS_100**
For [one who,] having practised this path of the highest reality (paramārtha), even without [fully] attaining [the goal of] yoga, [yet] partakes of the enjoyments of the world of the gods and, glad of mind, delights [there] for a very long time.
**PS_101**
Just as a universal emperor is honoured by all people among [the objects of] sense, so the yogin who has fallen [from practice] is honoured by all the gods throughout the worlds.
**PS_102**
Then, after a great length of time, having again attained human birth and practised yoga, he attains the divine nectar of immortality — from which he returns no more.
**PS_103**
Therefore whoever is intent upon this true path attains Śiva-hood. Knowing this, one should strive for the highest reality (paramārtha), by [whatever means,] this way or that.
**PS_104**

title: Paramārthasāra
text: For one who meditates upon this concise [exposition] uttered by Abhinavagupta, [which is] the supreme Brahman, Śiva-hood comes, before long, to enter into [pervade] his own heart.

title: Paramārthasāra
text: This most profoundly hidden essence of the scriptures has been compressed in a hundred āryā (the mātrā (moraic) meter of all 105 verses) verses by me, Abhinavagupta, made radiant by the remembrance of Śiva's feet.
